root.name: Bogo-Indian Defense: Haiti Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 Bb4+ 4. Bd2 Nc6

overview: In the Bogo-Indian after 4.Bd2 Black plays the unusual 4...Nc6 instead of the usual ...Qe7 or ...a5. White can trade bishops on d2 or keep the pin with 5.e3 and a quiet build-up. Play is positional and manoeuvring, with Black aiming for ...d5 or ...Bxd2 and ...Ne4.

white_ideas.idea: Trade on d2 and play e3, Be2, 0-0 for a small space edge
Fianchetto with g3 and Bg2 to pressure the centre
Prepare e4 or d5 to gain space

black_ideas.idea: Take the bishop on d2 and play ...d5 or ...Ne4 to reach a solid structure
Use Nc6 to pressure d4 and play ...e5
Keep a compact centre with ...O-O and ...d6

typical_structures.structure: Queen's Gambit-style centre with c4 and d4 against ...d5 or ...d6
Possible pawn doubling on d2 recaptures

character.notes: The Bogo-Indian is known for solid positions without early tactics.

soundness.notes: Sound; 4...Nc6 is a rare way to meet the check but not a mistake.

structure.notes: Pawns on c4/d4 against e6 leave the centre in tension; both sides can still choose their set-up.

approach.notes: An off-move-order of the Bogo-Indian, played rarely but by strong players.

level.notes: Plans are clear, with no long memorised lines.

character.reason: The Bogo-Indian structure is hard to break down and play is steady.

soundness.reason: The move is a rare but acceptable reply to Bd2.

structure.reason: The centre stays in tension and Black has not committed to d5 or d6.

approach.reason: Rare, but it is a respectable Bogo-Indian branch.

level.reason: Plans are straightforward and little needs memorising.

plans.reason: The fight is over centre space and who keeps the bishops.
